page: Microsoft Azure F16as_v6 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. It features 16 physical cores and 16 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz, supported by 64.0 GB of system memory, which equates to 4.0 GB per core. The CPU configuration includes a 32 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, alongside cryptography acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. The instance operates on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

This server does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable, allowing the attachment of high-performance external block storage. It does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the F16as_v6 demonstrates strong single-core performance, scoring in the top 25% for stress-ng single-core CPU tests and Geekbench single-core metrics. Multi-threaded performance is also robust, with bzip3 multi-threaded decompression and Geekbench multi-core scores placing in the top 25%. Text processing is a notable highlight, reaching the top 10% tier in Geekbench text processing benchmarks. Memory bandwidth and database operations, such as Redis SET and Passmark database tests, perform within the average range.

Given its dedicated AMD EPYC hardware profile and 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the F16as_v6 offers balanced resource density for general-purpose workloads. It is well-suited for applications requiring strong single-thread execution and moderate memory capacity, such as web serving, text processing pipelines, software compilation, and small-scale language model inference.
